title: Standardize incremental build manifests and decouple lint from primary CI pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Our CI runtime suffers from long builds and brittle lint steps that run on every push even for non-codepath changes. We have multiple cache regimes (Docker layer cache, BuildKit remote cache, and some ad-hoc s3 caches) without a clear manifest for incremental build inputs. This leads to inconsistent cache hits across platforms and noisy developer feedback loops.

Goal: Introduce a stable, repo-wide incremental build manifest format + canonical producer/consumer rules that allow deterministic cache keys across languages and platforms. At the same time, decouple lint/static analysis from the critical path of the heavy build+test pipeline by placing them in a fast, parallel pre-submit pipeline with targeted caching. The work should reduce median CI wall time by ~30% for typical PRs, improve cache hit-rate for rebuilds, and reduce time-to-feedback for lint failures.

Scope and deliverables:
- Design an "incremental-manifest.yaml" spec that lists inputs (source globs, toolchain versions, env variables) and outputs (image tags, artifacts) and a canonical algorithm for producing a content-hash key.
- Implement manifest generation hooks for TypeScript monorepo packages (pnpm), Go services, and Python components. Keep manifest generator idempotent and hermetic (pin SDK/toolchain versions).
- Wire BuildKit remote cache (CAS) keys to the manifest hash so layered caching is consistent across macOS/linux/arm runners.
- Create a separate lightweight CI job (lint-ci) that runs linters and formatters in parallel, uses targeted caching for linter caches, and emits structured lint reports to the console and the PR status.
- Update developer docs and add a conformance test that validates manifests produce identical keys on local dev and CI.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- We must avoid coupling this to any single CI provider; implement manifest and key algorithm in a provider-agnostic utility (go/python script) so it can run in Buildkite and GitHub Actions.
- Initially target common languages (TS/Go/Python); leave Rust/Ruby for follow-up to keep scope contained.
- The manifest hash must include toolchain pin information to avoid cache poisoning when SDKs change; this increases manifest churn on toolchain upgrades but preserves correctness.

Acceptance criteria:
- Incremental manifest spec published in the repo and PR template updated to require manifests for new packages.
- Buildkite CI shows a reproducible cache hit for a sample change set across linux/arm builders at least 80% of the time in staging.
- Lint pipeline returns results within 90s for 95% of PRs and no longer blocks the heavy build job by default.
- Documentation and a short dev walkthrough (README + 5-minute video) added to the developer handbook.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype manifest + key algo in a single service and verify cache stability (ENG-48654).
2) Implement language producers and BuildKit integration in parallel (ENG-48655).
3) Pilot on three mid-size repos, collect metrics for two weeks, and iterate.
4) Full repo rollout and PR template enforcement.

Notes: This ticket intersects with the cache consolidation work in ENG-31876 and the docker base convergence in ENG-24011. We should coordinate with Platform SRE to ensure cache storage capacity is provisioned for increased CAS usage.

2025-02-27 - Asha Patel: Decoupled lint pipeline merged into a parallel GitHub Actions workflow. Observed lint job median runtime 62s on contributors' sandbox. Docs updated: confluence.redwood.com/ci/incremental-manifests. Next: broader pilot and metric dashboard addition.
